lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Listen and say.

details: Listen and say introduces the target digraphs 'ng' and 'ck'. Students listen to the sounds and repeat them to practise correct mouth formation and pronunciation.
Look for attentive listening and clear, confident repetition of the nasal /ŋ/ and the plosive /k/ sounds.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Trace. Then write.

details: Trace and Write develops fine motor skills and letter formation. Students trace the digraphs to build muscle memory and write them independently to reinforce the spelling.
Look for correct pencil grip, neat formation of the letters within the lines, and keeping the letters close together to form a digraph.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Listen, point and say.

details: Listen, Point and Say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows they match the spoken word to the right image. Say practises pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing to the specific images (duck, ring, king, chick), and clear pronunciation of the ending sounds.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p67 - Say. Circle the letters that make the end sound.

details: Say and circle assesses phonemic discrimination. Students identify the object and circle the correct digraph corresponding to the ending sound.
Look for correct circling of 'ng' for Ring/King and 'ck' for Duck/Clock.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p67 - Trace and read.

details: Trace and read develops literacy and sentence structure awareness. Students trace the question "Have they got pasta?" to practise writing sight words and question forms.
Look for neat tracing of the letters and the ability to read the question aloud (supported by the teacher if needed).

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - 5. Complete the words.

details: Complete the words reinforces spelling and sound-symbol correspondence. Students fill in the missing 'ng' or 'ck' digraph to correctly spell the target vocabulary words.
Look for correct spelling of the four target words (duck, ring, king, chick) using the correct ending digraph.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - 6. Listen and read. Then trace.

details: Listen, read and trace combines auditory and kinesthetic learning. Students connect the spoken sentence to the written form, building sight-word recognition (have, they).
Look for students following the text as they listen, accurate tracing of the sentence "Have they got fish?", and attempts to read along.
